about.title: Who's behind GPUcloud.store?
about.subtitle: GPUcloud.store is built around a simple idea: high-performance infrastructure should be understandable, negotiable, and aligned with your business goals – not just your benchmarks.

text.intro: We are cloud consultants with a global Independent Datacenter network powered by Si Exchange.
text.mission: We sit at the intersection of technical infrastructure, commercial reality, and cross-border networks. That means helping you choose not just the "fastest hardware", but the architecture and partnerships that actually move your roadmap forward.
text.approach: With access to a broad network of independent datacenters and GPU providers, we help you navigate capacity, pricing, and reliability while keeping your teams focused on building products — not chasing hardware.

orchestration.title: Multi-cloud orchestration:
orchestration.text: Evaluate and design setups across major providers and specialized GPU clouds.

hybrid.title: Hybrid implementations:
hybrid.text: Combine on-prem or colocation hardware with cloud capacity in a way that doesn't become operational hell.

sourcing.title: Vendor & hardware sourcing:
sourcing.text: Help you navigate GPU availability, pricing, and trusted partners in independent datacenters worldwide.

alignment.title: Cost & growth alignment:
alignment.text: Translate infra decisions into KPI impact: throughput, latency, margin, and runway.

llmTraining.name: LLM Training
llmTraining.description: Large language model training and fine-tuning.

llmTraining.why: LLM training requires massive memory bandwidth and high compute throughput. Multi-GPU setups with fast interconnects reduce training time and keep utilization high.
considerations: Model size determines minimum VRAM requirements
Multi-GPU configurations need fast interconnects
Larger batch sizes improve training efficiency but require more memory
HBM memory delivers higher bandwidth than GDDR6

inference.why: Inference workloads prioritize low latency and cost efficiency with throughput per dollar.
considerations: Latency requirements determine GPU architecture choice
Throughput needs scale with request volume
INT8/FP16 precision reduces memory and increases speed
L40S offers strong price/performance for serving

computerVision.why: Computer vision needs balanced compute and memory for high-resolution images and video.
considerations: Image/video resolution determines VRAM needs
Batch processing benefits from larger VRAM
Real-time video requires low-latency GPUs
Training vs inference have different optimal configs

dataScience.why: Data science workloads benefit from GPU acceleration for dataframes, SQL, and ETL pipelines.
considerations: Dataset size determines memory requirements
RAPIDS acceleration requires CUDA-capable GPUs
Multi-GPU helps with larger-than-memory datasets
Storage I/O often bottlenecks before GPU

research.why: Research workloads require flexibility and access to new architectures for faster experimentation.
considerations: Latest architectures provide new capabilities
Flexibility to scale up or down per experiment
Mixed-precision support for diverse workloads
Fast iteration cycles are critical for research

development.why: Development environments need responsive GPUs for rapid iteration while keeping costs controlled.
considerations: Quick iteration cycles require responsive GPUs
Development workloads rarely need multi-GPU
Cost management matters for always-on instances
Should mirror production at smaller scale

llmTraining.enterprise: Large models (70B+ params), production training runs

computerVision.professional: High-res video processing, large model training
